newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-PowerGen posts higher H1, sets buyback.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-PowerGen posts higher H1, sets buyback.

text.p: British electricity generator PowerGen Plc posted higher first-half pretax profits on Thursday and said it would buy back up to 10 percent of its shares in coming weeks.

PowerGen's interim pretax profits rose four percent to 138 million pounds ($228 million), excluding an exceptional credit of 69 million pounds from the sale of its 21 percent stake in regional power company Midlands Electricity Plc.
Analysts had expected the firm to report pretax profits of 124 to 151 million pounds for the six months to September 29.
PowerGen also raised its interim dividend to 7.8 pence -- slightly higher than consensus estimates of 7.6 pence -- compared to 6.5 pence last year.
"We had a very strong performance from our UK business," finance director Peter Hickson told Reuters in an interview.
"There was a three percent increase in electricity demand, which was very much a reflection of a buoyant economy."
PowerGen's shares were up 2.5 pence at 553 by 1340 GMT after surging to an intraday high of 558 pence earlier.
"The fact that a share buyback is planned is positive, but equally the fact that there's no definite timescale may be seen as disappointing," one analyst said.
Hickson declined to give a deadline, adding that the firm had not set a cutoff date for the buyback's completion.
"We'll do it over the coming weeks, as and when the board feels it's appropriate. Clearly, we need to see a steady share price, and we need to determine when the moment is right.
"One would probably assume it's sooner rather than later, but that depends how you define sooner and later," he added, noting that the programme might be spread out over months.
The buyback plan came amid market speculation about PowerGen's strategy after its 1.95 billion pound bid for Midlands was blocked by British regulators this year.

"We believe that, having reviewed our balance sheet, the share buyback offers the best deal for our shareholders," Hickson said, adding that the company was continually looking at potential projects and acquisitions.
"We have a number of things we are reviewing. There are no plans to move forward at this stage," he said.
According to its balance sheet, PowerGen spent about 346 million pounds in the first-half on share buybacks.

Hickson said the company was not currently planning any acquisition on the scale of its Midlands offer, adding that it was unlikely it would try to bid for another of Britain's independent regional electricity companies.
Hickson said the company expected to take a provision in the second half related to its 50-percent liability on long-term gas supply contracts signed by its Kinetica gas joint venture.
However, he did not expect the provision to offset the company's first-half gain from the sale of its Midlands stake.
Kinetica, which traded at a loss in the first half, is owned by PowerGen and Conoco (UK), a unit of DuPont Co.
Regarding contractual cover, PowerGen said it was fully-contracted for all its expected output in 1996/1997.
"We feel that this could be another good year of progress. We're optimistic that our performance for the full year will be very acceptable," he said. ($1=.6054 Pound)
